_comment: domain -> where to report. URLs are STARTING POINTS and must be re-verified before production use; platforms move these pages often.

entries.name: Google Search
entries.notes: Removal of non-consensual explicit / involuntary fake imagery from Search results.

entries.name: Facebook (Meta)
entries.notes: Report the post/profile in-app first; search the Help Center for 'intimate images'. Also use StopNCII.

entries.name: Instagram (Meta)
entries.notes: Use in-app 'Report' on the post/profile; also StopNCII.

entries.name: TikTok
entries.notes: In-app report is fastest; the web form is the fallback.

entries.name: X (Twitter)
entries.notes: Report the post; use the sensitive-media / non-consensual nudity form from the Help Center.

entries.name: Pornhub (Aylo)
entries.notes: Use the content-removal / non-consensual content request from the Help Center.

entries.name: XVideos / XNXX
entries.notes: Use the 'Content removal' / 'Report' link in the site footer; if none works, contact the hosting provider (see abuse lookup).

entries.name: Telegram
entries.notes: Email abuse@telegram.org with the message links.

entries.name: Imgur
entries.notes: Use the report link on the post.

entries.name: Pinterest
entries.notes: Report the Pin from the ... menu.

entries.name: YouTube
entries.notes: Report the video, or use the privacy-complaint process.

entries.name: Wikimedia
entries.notes: Request deletion or contact Wikimedia Trust & Safety.

fallback.name: Unknown site
fallback.notes: 1) Look for 'Report / DMCA / Content removal' in the footer. 2) Find the host with a WHOIS / hosting lookup and email its abuse contact. 3) Ask Google to de-list the URL from Search.
